name: Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba

findings.controller: Alcatel Submarine Networks (France), end-to-end supplier of the CELIA trunk; supplier of the Bonaire branch not stated
findings.local_actor: Saba Statia Cable System BV (SSCS, 100% Dutch state-owned), contracting with SETAR N.V. (Aruba) as CELIA initiator
findings.financier: Dutch government via SSCS; EU CEF Digital grant (scope disputed between sources)
findings.summary: State-owned SSCS signed an agreement with Aruba's SETAR to connect Bonaire to the CELIA submarine cable (Aruba, Martinique, Antigua, Puerto Rico, Florida), targeted operational late 2027; a seabed survey began August 2025.

sources.publisher: Rijksdienst Caribisch Nederland (Government of the Netherlands)

findings.analyst_inference: Pole third rests on ASN (France) being named CELIA's end-to-end supplier in Dec 2024 (SubTel Forum); none of the Bonaire sources name the branch supplier, so the controller of the Bonaire segment is inferred. Corroborated: Rijksdienst (S1) plus BES Reporter (S3, own quotes from three parties). Tier 3 because an SSCS-SETAR agreement is signed, though no value is given. Rijksdienst says the project is partly EU CEF-funded; BES Reporter ties the CEF money to the Curacao connection. EUR 4m fibre subsidy to local telcos is separate and not coded.

findings.controller: Not stated (equipment vendor of the SSCS cable unknown); capacity provider is Saba Statia Cable System BV (Dutch state-owned)
findings.local_actor: EUTEL N.V. and Government of St. Eustatius
findings.summary: St. Eustatius government and operator EUTEL concluded a five-year IP-transit agreement on the SSCS submarine cable, owned by the Dutch Interior Ministry, linking Statia and Saba to St. Maarten, St. Barts and St. Kitts, with planned Miami routes.

sources.publisher: Rijksdienst Caribisch Nederland (Government of the Netherlands)

findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: under the equipment-vendor rule the controller is whoever supplied the SSCS cable and terminal equipment, which no source opened names. Owner-operator is the Dutch state (domestic, since BES is part of the Netherlands). Five-year term from late 2020 may expire about 2025; not reconfirmed. Single opened S1, so medium.

findings.local_actor: Korps Politie Caribisch Nederland (KPCN); C3 as regional rollout partner
findings.summary: The Dutch Caribbean Police Force deployed ZEPCAM T3 Live body-worn cameras with live video streaming, audio and GPS across Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, rolled out by regional partner C3. No AI analytics or back-end platform described.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole domestic assumes ZEPCAM is a Netherlands company (background knowledge; the article does not state nationality) and BES is part of the Netherlands. Tier 5 because the article describes the system as implemented, but number of cameras and contract value are not given. Body-worn video is police surveillance, not AI analytics; reviewer may judge it out of scope. Single opened S2 source.

facilities.null_reason: two searches (English and Dutch) found no data-centre or AI-campus project in Bonaire, Sint Eustatius or Saba; only a 2014 utility ICT refresh and regional Curacao items

silicon.null_reason: no dedicated search; no accelerator purchase or deployment surfaced in facilities or models searches

models.null_reason: one Dutch-language search found no frontier-model partnership, government AI adoption or sovereign model specific to the Caribbean Netherlands

research_gaps: RAN/core equipment vendors for Bonaire mobile operators (Digicel Bonaire, Flow/Kla, Telbo) and for Satel (Saba) and EUTEL (Statia); Digicel's 2017 ZTE LTE deal covered 26 unnamed markets, Bonaire inclusion not established.
Supplier of the CELIA Bonaire (and Curacao) branch and whether a supply contract and value were published; confirm the scope of EU CEF Digital co-financing.
Supplier of the SSCS cable system (Saba-Statia) and whether the 2020 EUTEL IP-transit agreement was renewed; status of the planned direct Miami routes.
Camera/VMS vendors for public CCTV in Bonaire and Statia (temporary carnival surveillance reported by InfoBonaire and BES Reporter, not opened); check for Hikvision/Dahua.
ZEPCAM contract value, camera count and where live-stream video is hosted.
Whether the Dutch national AI/cloud policies (e.g. government cloud rules) apply in the BES islands and to which providers.
